window.clock: 244 trading days; each book's own published execution lag is kept
window.how_chosen: intersection of the three published daily series

carry_basis_only.definition: the basis move net of cost -- no index exposure, no hedge, no account

carry_excess_hedged.definition: the same day minus the same notional's index return -- the residual a hedge leaves

carry_unhedged.definition: per-lot daily points on the held contract -- carries the index's own vol

capital_return_identity.rule: expected return on capital = target vol x Sharpe (a vol-targeted book holds vol fixed)
capital_return_identity.note: printed because the casual comparison is a Sharpe: a reader who multiplies sees why the basis line's 3.19 cannot turn into a 25% book

sentence: On one window (2020-01-03..2026-11-26) and one clock the three books print 9.94% / 6.34% / 10.22% (ETF / CB / carry basis). The carry line wins and cannot be bought: it is the basis arm, quoted per notional, and the family's own hedged arm on the same leg is 1.42 Sharpe, not 2.97. At the book's 8.0% vol target one IC lot still needs 1,137,862 CNY of capital against a 1,000,000 CNY wallet, so the executable line is 0 lots.
what_this_face_does_not_do: it re-prices nothing and re-runs no rule; it slices three published daily series onto one calendar and reads the published sizing faces for the capital arithmetic
caveats: the carry arm is a daily excess return on notional; the ETF/CB books are returns on capital
the carry row's sharpe on this common window is not the family's published 2.97 — that one is the 2017-2026 IC-only window; the two differ because the window differs, not because the rule changed
2020-01..2022-07 the carry arm is IC only (IM listed 2022-07-25); after that it is the mean of the two legs
the ETF book's vol target makes its drawdown a dial, so its return is not a fair 'more risk more return' comparison
costs: ETF/CB 10bp per side as published, carry 1.5bp per side as published
